subject: Control mapping: retention + audit logging evidence (SOC2/ISO) — finalize v1 + repeatable collection steps
body:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Daniel Carter <daniel.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Hanae Suzuki <hanae.suzuki@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 10, 2025 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Control mapping: retention + audit logging evidence (SOC2/ISO) — finalize v1 + repeatable collection steps

Team —

We need to lock v1 of the retention + audit logging control mapping this week so Daniel can fold it into the compliance reporting pack and we have a repeatable evidence procedure for audits + customer requests.

Two asks:
1) Please review the draft mapping matrix (attached) and add comments by EOD Wed.
2) Confirm the evidence collection steps are realistic/repeatable and identify any “manual-only” steps we should automate in the next sprint.

Confluence pages we’re anchoring on (please keep evidence pointers consistent with these):
- Control mapping page: confluence://security-and-compliance/compliance-evidence/control-mapping-retention-and-audit-logging
- Reporting pack outline: confluence://security-and-compliance/compliance-evidence/compliance-reporting-pack-v1
- Retention overview: confluence://security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/retention-controls-overview
- Audit log retention + exports: confluence://security-and-compliance/audit-logging/audit-log-retention-and-exports
- Exceptions/legal holds: confluence://security-and-compliance/risk-and-exceptions/retention-exceptions-and-legal-holds-process
- Enforcement runbook: confluence://eng-platform/runbooks/retention-enforcement-job-runbook

Key open questions in the draft (highlighted in yellow):
- For telemetry/analytics tables that are eligible for TTL: what’s the “system of record” evidence? (dashboard screenshots vs config export vs query output)
- How are we documenting legal hold activation + periodic review in a way we can show auditors without leaking sensitive case details?
- For “policy changes”: do we want to standardize on “Console audit events + control plane DB record” as evidence, or is Console audit trail sufficient?

Attachments:
- Retention_Audit_Control-Mapping_v1.0_draft.xlsx
- Evidence_Collection_Procedure_Retention-Audit_v0.3.docx

Thanks,
Olga
—
Olga Petrov
GRC / Compliance Lead
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Daniel Carter <daniel.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Hanae Suzuki <hanae.suzuki@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 10, 2025 at 10:03 AM PST
Subject: Re: Control mapping: retention + audit logging evidence (SOC2/ISO) — finalize v1 + repeatable collection steps

Reviewed the draft quickly — overall looks good.

Security Eng notes (esp. if we’re aligning to SOC 2 CC7 / ISO A.8 logging):

1) Audit log integrity / tamper-resistance
- In the mapping, I’d avoid language implying “immutable” unless we can formally back it up.
- Better: “append-only service semantics + restricted write access + monitoring for anomalies.”
- Evidence: IAM/RBAC policy excerpt (who can write), plus query output showing audit events are only created by the audit logging service.

2) Legal holds
- For evidence: we can show that legal hold flags exist and that enforcement respects holds.
- But we should NOT share case-level details. Suggest: evidence is a redacted export of the holds table (IDs + timestamps + hold state), plus the runbook for approvals/review.

3) Change management
- For retention policy changes: I agree with “Console audit events + control plane record” as the strongest pairing.
- Console audit trail alone is risky if auditors ask how it’s derived.

If you want, I can add suggested control statements into the spreadsheet later today.

Marcus

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Daniel Carter <daniel.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Hanae Suzuki <hanae.suzuki@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 10, 2025 at 11:21 AM PST
Subject: Re: Control mapping: retention + audit logging evidence (SOC2/ISO) — finalize v1 + repeatable collection steps

On telemetry/analytics TTL evidence:

What we can reliably produce in v1:
- “Source of truth” = dataset/table TTL configuration from the warehouse + the PR/migration that introduced/changed it.
- We can add a script output (timestamped) that prints TTL settings for the in-scope tables and attaches it to the evidence snapshot.

What I’d avoid using as primary evidence:
- Dashboard screenshots alone (too easy to drift / not authoritative).

Also: confirm which tables are *in* v1. The draft includes:
- request_metadata_agg
- token_usage_daily
- model_latency_p95

Those are fine. But some operational logs are managed per SRE standards/vendor limits and shouldn’t be described as tenant-configurable (I saw one row that might imply that).

If you want, I can provide a list of “eligible for tenant retention” vs “platform/SRE governed” for the mapping sheet.

Logan

From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Daniel Carter <daniel.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Hanae Suzuki <hanae.suzuki@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 10, 2025 at 1:08 PM PST
Subject: Re: Control mapping: retention + audit logging evidence (SOC2/ISO) — finalize v1 + repeatable collection steps

On the “policy changes evidence” question:

Recommended evidence bundle (repeatable):
1) Export of effective retention policy for a tenant (via control plane admin endpoint) including:
- tenant_id
- policy version
- per-data-type retention days
- legal hold override status
- updated_at + updated_by (actor)

2) Matching Console audit event(s) for policy updates
- includes actor, timestamp, diff summary

3) Link to the change record (PR/Linear) when the change is system-default / schema-related (not tenant-config)

We can make (1) deterministic and easy to snapshot, which helps a lot for auditors.

Re: legal holds: the enforcement worker consults the hold flags; we can provide test artifacts that show “hold => no delete.” Not sure if you want that in the evidence pack v1, but it’s good for internal audit readiness.

Ethan

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Daniel Carter <daniel.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Hanae Suzuki <hanae.suzuki@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 10, 2025 at 2:37 PM PST
Subject: Re: Control mapping: retention + audit logging evidence (SOC2/ISO) — finalize v1 + repeatable collection steps

+1 to the approach.

Product clarifications for the control statements / pack language:
- Please make it explicit that tenant-configurable retention applies to specific datasets (audit logs, admin activity, request metadata, eligible telemetry tables) and is subject to guardrails (min/max, legal hold).
- We should avoid saying “all logs” or “all telemetry” in any customer-facing statement.
- Default retention values vary by deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) and in Private some controls may be customer-operated, so evidence may be “deployment configuration + customer attestation” rather than “our hosted console screenshot.”

If you send me the specific control statements you plan to include, I can sanity-check for product accuracy / wording.

Naomi

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Daniel Carter <daniel.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Hanae Suzuki <hanae.suzuki@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 10, 2025 at 4:48 PM PST
Subject: Re: Control mapping: retention + audit logging evidence (SOC2/ISO) — finalize v1 + repeatable collection steps

Thanks all — this is exactly what I needed.

Decisions / updates I’m making to the mapping based on replies:
- Replace “immutable audit logs” phrasing with Marcus’ recommended language (append-only semantics + restricted write access + monitoring).
- Telemetry TTL evidence will be: (a) TTL config export/script output + (b) PR/migration reference. Dashboards/screenshots will be “supporting” only.
- Legal hold evidence will be a redacted holds export + the approvals/review runbook (no case details).
- Policy change evidence will be standardized as: control plane policy export + Console audit event(s). (Ethan: I’m taking your proposed bundle.)

Action items:
1) Logan — please send a short list of telemetry datasets that are “tenant retention eligible” vs “platform/SRE governed” so I can correct the one ambiguous row. Even 5–10 bullets is fine.
2) Marcus — if you can drop suggested control statement text into the spreadsheet by Wed, I’ll merge.
3) Naomi — I’ll send you the final customer-facing control statements for a quick wording pass before we publish to the reporting pack.
4) Daniel — once I post v1 of the mapping to Confluence, please reference it from the compliance reporting pack v1 (confluence://security-and-compliance/compliance-evidence/compliance-reporting-pack-v1) and align the evidence snapshot process to it. ENG-2940 is the right home for the generator work.

I’ll update the Confluence mapping page tomorrow with:
- control-to-evidence matrix
- “evidence collection procedure” (repeatable steps + required artifacts)
- owners and cadence

Olga
—
Olga Petrov
GRC / Compliance Lead
Redwood Inference
